Profile

Diagnostics, science, and implementation in one professional profile

I am an Associate Professor and medical immunologist at UMC Utrecht. I lead transplantation diagnostics within the Central Diagnostic Laboratory and work at the interface of routine care, translational immunology, immunogenetics, and clinical data innovation.

Publications 129 Citations 5,043 h-index 45 ORCID 0000-0001-9441-1019

My mission is to ensure that every transplant patient achieves the best possible outcome by embedding advanced immunogenetic matching and innovative diagnostics into daily clinical practice.

My scientific work addresses how donor-recipient immunogenetic differences shape allo-immunity and transplant outcome. This includes HLA typing, antibody diagnostics, indirect HLA epitope recognition, PIRCHE-based risk assessment, donor-specific antibodies, graft rejection, graft failure, and immune monitoring after transplantation.

A consistent principle in my work is that novel analytical methods should move beyond proof of concept. They must be interpretable, technically robust, compatible with laboratory quality systems, and connected to clinical workflows.

Scientific focus

Four connected fields of work

My focus combines high-quality transplantation diagnostics with mechanistic research, computational matching, and implementation into clinical and laboratory systems.

01

HLA diagnostics

I lead accredited HLA typing and antibody diagnostics, including clinical interpretation, donor-recipient compatibility assessment, donor-specific antibody evaluation, and direct consultation with transplant teams.

02

Epitope matching

I quantify immunological compatibility through indirect T-cell epitope recognition, PIRCHE-II, B-cell epitope concepts, and combined risk models for rejection and graft outcome.

03

Data standards

I develop interoperable representations for HLA and antibody data, including GL String, HML, HAML, and related structures that support reproducible exchange between laboratories, registries, software, and research systems.

04

Implementation

I translate assays, algorithms, and data models into validated workflows, interpretable reports, decision support, and infrastructure for routine transplantation care.

Selected initiatives

Programs connecting research, diagnostics and implementation

These initiatives translate immunogenetic concepts, laboratory expertise and interoperable data into practical improvements for transplantation care.

01

PIRCHE

I develop and clinically evaluate indirect T-cell epitope matching to improve donor-recipient risk assessment and transplant outcome prediction.

02

HAML and HLA data standards

I contribute to structured, interoperable exchange of HLA and antibody data between laboratories, registries, research platforms and clinical systems.

03

EFI BITCom

As founding chair, I support bioinformatics, education and international harmonization across the European histocompatibility and immunogenetics community.

04

Data-driven diagnostics and AI

I develop operational analytics, workflow intelligence and decision support to improve laboratory quality, capacity and clinical interpretation.

05

Matchis secondment

My secondment connects donor registry practice with HLA expertise, research development and implementation of improved matching strategies.

Career

From molecular HLA typing to integrated transplantation diagnostics

Current

UMC Utrecht

Associate Professor, medical immunologist, and Director Transplantation Diagnostics within the Central Diagnostic Laboratory.

Academic development

Transplantation immunology and immunogenetics

I developed a research line integrating donor-recipient matching, PIRCHE, antibody risk, immune monitoring, computational models, and clinical implementation.

Postdoctoral period

Minor histocompatibility antigens

I conducted postdoctoral research in the laboratory of Els Goulmy, expanding my expertise from HLA into cellular allo-immunity and minor histocompatibility antigens.

Education

Leiden University Medical Center

I completed an MSc in Biomedical Sciences and a PhD in Immunology. My first practical HLA experience was in 1992 through PCR-SSOP work with Marius Giphart.
